problem: Prior GNN-based target-driven navigation methods map observations to actions end-to-end using incomplete relation graphs, mostly restricted to single-room settings (AI2-THOR). They are not interpretable and generalize poorly, ignoring room connectivity and object-in-room membership in multi-room houses.
motivation: Domestic robots must find objects in unknown multi-room houses, and humans exploit priors such as room types, object-in-room membership and house layout. SLAM-based and end-to-end methods struggle with semantic maps, generalization, and balancing exploitation and exploration. Decoupling reasoning, planning and control allows dedicated design and interpretability.
key_idea: A hierarchical framework that uses GNN-extracted object/region/layout priors and UCT bandit reasoning over a multi-layer semantic topological graph to pick semantic sub-goals, converted to spatial goals by an online Voronoi local graph and executed by a pretrained PointNav controller.
insight: The ablations show that relationship priors are the dominant factor for success rate (SR drops from 62.5 to 25.0 without priors), while the UCT bonus and distance penalty mainly improve path efficiency (SPL 0.102 to 0.034 and 0.030 respectively without them). Separating prior learning from control in a hierarchy beats learning a semantically-aware policy end-to-end. Continuous mode (retaining the topological memory) raises SR to 85.7 but lowers SPL by favoring exploitation.
method: Object embedding: unsupervised edge-weighted GraphSAGE on an object graph from Matterport3D with GloVe initial features, negative-sampling loss, and per-category mean embeddings
Region embedding: self-supervised GCN over object-embedding sub-graphs, with a loss combining object-in-region membership and region-label classification

Region Rollout: a conditional GraphRNN (GRU/LSTM) over region-embedding sequences with edge masks that predicts the embeddings and labels of unseen neighboring regions (ghost nodes), trained with cross-entropy

UCT reasoner: builds a multi-layer topological graph (object, clique, vertex, ghost) and scores nodes V = mean descendant inductive bias + c1*sqrt(ln N/n) - c2*L_dis (c1=1, c2=0.5), enabling backtracking ('regret')
Online Voronoi local graph: projects depth-reconstructed obstacles to 2D, clusters with DBSCAN into convex hulls, builds Delaunay/Voronoi to convert semantic sub-goals into relative coordinates
Low-level controller and front-end: YOLOv4 fine-tuned on Matterport3D for detection; pretrained occupancy-anticipation PointNav policy executes actions

setting.backbone: YOLOv4 (fine-tuned) + GraphSAGE/GCN/GraphRNN relation networks + UCT + pretrained occupancy-anticipation PointNav controller
setting.training_data: Matterport3D object and region annotations (90 houses, 40 object categories, 31 region labels) for relation networks and detector; controller pretrained on PointNav
setting.action_space: low-level Habitat actions from a PointNav controller, given relative-coordinate sub-goals from the Voronoi planner
setting.privileged: none stated at test time (map-less), though object/region priors are learned from Matterport3D ground-truth annotations

numbers_note: The paper does not state which split or how many episodes were used. 'MP3D-ObjNav val-unseen' is an assumption. SPL is printed as a 0-1 fraction (not percent). The text says 19 target categories in the ReVoLT-i row, while the setup lists 21.
results: ReVoLT-i small reaches 66.7% SR and 0.265 SPL versus SemExp's 36.0% SR and 0.144 SPL (about 80% relative SR gain, nearly 2x SPL). Standard ReVoLT-i (62.5 SR) and continuous ReVoLT-c (85.7 SR) also beat SemExp, Active Neural SLAM (32.1) and DD-PPO (6.2).
limitations: Evaluation protocol is unclear (episode count and split unspecified, small sample sizes implied by values like 66.7/85.7), and SemExp numbers were copied from its paper rather than re-run
Region Rollout prediction accuracy is only 45%, and the pipeline depends on ground-truth Matterport3D annotations for priors and on a fine-tuned detector
Continuous mode lowers SPL, and SPL of the standard mode is low (0.102) despite high SR
